key_insight: The paper argues that medical AI should move from static diagnosis toward “world models” that learn patient-state dynamics and simulate how disease may change under different interventions.
clinical_relevance: Such models could help clinicians anticipate deterioration, compare treatment-conditioned futures, and better tailor care to individual patients.
method: Construct patient-state representations from longitudinal and multimodal medical data.
Model clinical dynamics to simulate disease progression over time.
Use intervention decision support to compare potential treatment paths and guide planning.
evidence_signal: This is a review and roadmap paper, so the evidence comes from synthesizing representative systems across foundation models, longitudinal modelling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins rather than from a new clinical dataset.
watch_item: A key concern is that plausible simulated rollouts may not be clinically reliable without rigorous validation, calibration, and careful integration into decision-making workflows.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
